breakfast.name: Roti and Curry
instructions: Make roti dough, rest
Roll thin circles
Cook on tawa, brush with oil
Serve with curry
breakfast.description: Fijian-Indian breakfast — fresh roti with curry.

breakfast.name: Cassava with Coconut Cream
instructions: Peel and boil cassava until tender
Drizzle with warm coconut cream
Sprinkle salt and sugar

breakfast.name: Roti Paratha with Dhal (Indo-Fijian Breakfast)
ingredients: Roti: 2 cups flour, water, salt, ghee or oil
Dhal: red lentils, turmeric, cumin, garlic, onion, tomato, chili
instructions: Make roti dough with flour, water, salt — rest 20 min
Roll out, brush with ghee, fold into layers, roll again — this creates flaky layers
Cook on hot tava/griddle until golden and flaky on both sides
For dhal: cook red lentils with turmeric until soft and breaking down
Temper with ghee, cumin seeds, garlic, onion, tomato, chili — pour over dhal
Serve flaky roti with dhal for dipping
Indo-Fijians brought this tradition from India in the 1800s — it's now as Fijian as kokoda
The layered roti technique is an art — grandmother hands vs. beginner hands, there's a difference
breakfast.description: Indo-Fijian flaky roti with spiced lentil dhal — brought to Fiji by Indian laborers in the 1800s and now an integral part of Fijian food culture. The roti-flipping technique and the fusion of Indian and Pacific cultures on one plate have made Indo-Fijian breakfast a viral food-heritage story.

lunch.name: Kokoda (Fijian Ceviche)
instructions: Marinate fish in lime juice 20 min
Drain excess juice
Add coconut cream, tomato, onion, chili
Toss gently, garnish with cilantro
Serve cold in coconut shell
lunch.description: Fiji's signature dish — raw fish 'cooked' in lime and coconut cream.

lunch.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut)
instructions: Layer taro leaves, fill with coconut cream and onion
Wrap in foil or banana leaves
Bake or steam in lovo (earth oven) 2 hours
lunch.description: Taro leaves slow-cooked in rich coconut cream.

lunch.name: Kokoda (Fijian Raw Fish Salad)
ingredients: 500g fresh mahi-mahi or walu (Spanish mackerel) — sushi-grade fresh
instructions: Cut fish into small cubes
Marinate in lime juice for 2-3 hours in the fridge — the acid 'cooks' the fish until opaque
Drain off most of the lime juice
Mix in coconut cream — the fish turns creamy and rich
Add tomato, onion, chili, cucumber
Season with salt
Serve in a halved coconut shell — this is the traditional and viral presentation
The fish should be 'cooked' through from the lime but silky from the coconut cream
This is Fiji's national dish — every resort, every village, every celebration has kokoda
lunch.description: Fiji's national dish — raw fish 'cooked' in lime juice and dressed in coconut cream, served in a halved coconut shell. The Pacific islands' answer to ceviche. The coconut-shell presentation and the lime-to-cream transformation have made kokoda one of the most viral Pacific Island dishes worldwide.

lunch.name: Fiji Chop Suey (Indo-Chinese-Fijian Fusion)
ingredients: Egg noodles or chow mein noodles
Mixed vegetables: cabbage, carrot, bell pepper, bean sprouts
Protein: chicken, shrimp, or char siu pork
instructions: Cook noodles, drain
Stir-fry protein with garlic and ginger in hot wok
Add vegetables — keep them crispy
Add cooked noodles, toss with soy sauce, oyster sauce
Finish with sesame oil and green onion
Fiji's chop suey is a unique fusion — Chinese technique, Indian spicing, Pacific ingredients
Every Fijian-Chinese restaurant has their version — it's comfort food that unites all of Fiji's communities
Often includes a side of chili sauce unique to Fijian-Chinese cooking
lunch.description: Fiji's unique contribution to chop suey — a Chinese-Indian-Pacific fusion born from the multicultural melting pot of the islands. Every Fijian-Chinese restaurant has their version. The three-culture fusion story (Indian laborers, Chinese merchants, Pacific Islanders) makes Fijian chop suey a viral food-history moment.

imageCredit.author: Eli Hodapp from Naperville, United States

dinner.name: Lovo Feast (Earth Oven)
instructions: Dig pit, heat rocks
Wrap meats and vegetables in banana leaves
Layer over hot rocks
Cover with earth
Cook 3 hours
Unwrap and serve communally

dinner.name: Fish Suruwa (Fish Curry)
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, ginger
Add turmeric, chili, tomato
Add coconut milk, simmer
Add fish, cook gently 15 min
dinner.description: Fijian fish curry in coconut milk.

dinner.name: Lovo (Underground Earth Oven Feast)
ingredients: Whole pig or large cuts of pork
Root vegetables: taro, cassava, sweet potato, breadfruit
Palusami: taro leaves wrapped around coconut cream
instructions: Dig a pit, build a fire, heat volcanic stones until white-hot
Line the pit with hot stones
Wrap meats and vegetables individually in banana leaves
Layer wrapped parcels on the hot stones — heaviest items closest to the heat
Cover everything with more banana leaves, then burlap sacks, then earth
Seal completely — no steam should escape
Cook underground for 3-4 hours — the earth oven steams and smokes everything simultaneously
Unearth the feast — the dramatic reveal is the communal moment
Everything comes out smoky, tender, and infused with the earthy, herbal aroma of banana leaves
This is Fiji's ultimate celebration cooking — weddings, holidays, village gatherings all center on lovo
dinner.description: Fiji's underground earth oven feast — an entire meal of pork, chicken, root vegetables, and coconut-cream-stuffed taro leaves cooked on hot volcanic stones buried under earth for hours. The dramatic unearthing moment, when the banana-leaf parcels are revealed steaming and tender, is the most spectacular food video from the Pacific Islands.

dinner.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut Cream)
ingredients: Tinned corned beef (optional — the Pacific Island pantry staple)
instructions: Layer taro leaves, removing thick stems
Place onion and optional corned beef in the center
Pour coconut cream over the leaves
Wrap tightly in banana leaves — multiple layers to seal
Bake in oven at 175°C for 1 hour, or in an underground lovo
The taro leaves soften and become silky, absorbing the coconut cream
The result is like the Pacific Island version of creamed spinach — but richer
Unwrap at the table — the steaming coconut-leaf parcel is the moment
dinner.description: Taro leaves slow-baked in coconut cream until silky and rich — Fiji's essential side dish, often cooked in the underground lovo oven. The banana-leaf parcel unwrapping and the coconut-cream-saturated leaves are viral Pacific Island food content. Sometimes includes corned beef — a beloved Pacific pantry staple.

snacks.name: Kora (Coconut Bread)
instructions: Mix flour, coconut, sugar, baking powder
Add coconut milk
Pour into pan, bake at 180°C 30 min

snacks.name: Cassava Chips (Fijian-Style)
instructions: Peel cassava, slice very thin — mandoline-thin if possible
Soak in cold water 30 min to remove excess starch
Dry thoroughly — wet cassava splatters dangerously in oil
Deep fry in batches at 170°C until golden and crispy — 3-4 min
Drain, season immediately with salt, chili, lemon juice
These are crunchier and more satisfying than potato chips
Cassava is Fiji's staple root — it grows everywhere and feeds everyone
Street vendors sell these in paper cones at every market
snacks.description: Fijian cassava chips — crunchier and more satisfying than potato chips, fried thin and seasoned with salt, chili, and lemon. Cassava is the Pacific Islands' staple root, and these chips at every market stall are the snack that travelers remember most. The crunch-comparison to potato chips always goes viral.

snacks.name: Roti Wrap (Fijian Street Food)
ingredients: Curry filling: chicken, lamb, or vegetable curry
instructions: Warm the roti
Spoon curry filling down the center
Add chutneys and pickled vegetables
Roll up tight — eat like a burrito
This is Fiji's most popular street food — every town has roti wrap vendors
The Indo-Fijian community brought this tradition and it became universal Fijian fast food
Often sold from roadside stands and small shops called 'roti houses'
snacks.description: Fiji's most popular street food — warm roti wrapped around curry with chutneys, eaten like a burrito. Born from the Indo-Fijian community and adopted by everyone on the islands. Roti house culture is a viral part of Fiji's food story — proof that the islands' food is as Indian as it is Pacific.

desserts.name: Vakalolo (Cassava Coconut Pudding)
instructions: Mix cassava, coconut, sugar
Add coconut cream
Wrap in banana leaves
Steam or bake 60 min
desserts.description: Dense, sweet cassava and coconut pudding steamed in banana leaves.

desserts.name: Vakalolo (Cassava and Coconut Pudding)
ingredients: 1/2 cup brown sugar or grated palm sugar
instructions: Grate fresh cassava
Mix with coconut cream and sugar
Wrap portions in banana leaf parcels
Steam for 25-30 min until set and sticky
Unwrap — the pudding should be dense, sweet, and coconut-rich
The banana leaf infuses a subtle grassy, herbal aroma
Can also be baked in a pan if banana leaves aren't available
This is Fiji's traditional sweet — every village kitchen knows vakalolo
desserts.description: Fiji's traditional coconut-cassava pudding — grated cassava mixed with coconut cream and palm sugar, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed. Dense, sweet, and deeply coconutty. The banana-leaf wrapping and the Pacific Island ingredient simplicity make vakalolo a viral representation of Oceanian dessert tradition.

desserts.name: Kovu (Coconut Caramel)
instructions: Cook sugar and water until it becomes a golden caramel
Add grated coconut — stir constantly as it toasts in the caramel
Cook until the coconut is golden and coated in caramel — 10-15 min
Add vanilla and salt
Drop spoonfuls onto parchment or banana leaf to set
The coconut gets chewy and crunchy in the caramel — like tropical brittle
These are sold at every market in Fiji — the simplest sweet on the islands
The fresh coconut makes all the difference — dried coconut won't give the same texture
desserts.description: Fiji's simplest sweet — freshly grated coconut toasted in caramel until golden and crunchy. Sold at every market in the islands. The two-ingredient simplicity (coconut + sugar) and the tropical-brittle texture make kovu a viral example of how Pacific Island desserts need nothing but what the palm trees provide.

drinks.name: Kava (Yaqona)
instructions: Mix pounded kava with water in tanoa (bowl)
Strain through cloth
Serve in coconut shell cups
Clap once before drinking, three times after
drinks.description: Earthy, ceremonial kava drink — Fiji's social ritual.

drinks.name: Fresh Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open young coconut
Pour water into glass
Serve chilled
drinks.description: Nature's isotonic drink, straight from the coconut.
